svg.text: WHERE TENANT IDENTITY COMES FROM (never the request payload for tenant roles)
Interactive: JWT → User row
users.tenant_id of the authenticated user;
?tenantId honoured for super_admin only
Telephony: dialed number
phone_numbers row anchors the tenant;
botId may only pick a bot inside that tenant
Voice runtime: minted session
API writes tenant into voice:session:{id};
worker consumes, never mints (4403 on mismatch)
MCP: verified JWT contextvar
identity from the token middleware only —
tool arguments can never set the tenant
ENFORCEMENT POINTS (server-side; frontend gates are affordances)
API list queries — resolve_tenant_id()
tenant role + foreign tenantId → 403; unlinked account → 403;
super_admin must name a tenant explicitly (400 otherwise)
46 call sites across routers
API by-id access — assert_tenant_access()
cross-tenant row → NotFoundError (404, never 403) so foreign
record existence is not leaked · 49 call sites
create/update guards block role escalation + cross-tenant refs
Knowledge plane — two layers
authorize_kb_ids: bot-scoped ∪ tenant ∪ global KBs, any miss →
404 without naming which id failed
pgvector _tenant_clause re-filters tenant_id inside every SQL read/write
Financial visibility — costs.view
cost / pricing / spend fields nulled in serializers, analytics,
conversation detail and exports for roles without the permission
(tenant_user has no costs.view; reports refuse financial exports)
Data model — tenant_id columns, per-query discipline
TenantOwnedMixin (NOT NULL FK + index) on 5 models; ~25 more tables carry tenant_id declared inline; global/shared rows use tenant_id NULL
(platform voices, global KBs, platform compliance templates). Tenant deletes are soft; hard delete is env-gated.
No ORM-level global tenant filter exists — isolation depends on every query using the helpers above (verified risk, see §24).
Audit: every mutation writes an audit row with tenant_id; tenant admins can read only their tenant's slice of /audit.
WORKED EXAMPLE — TENANT A → TENANT B

g.text: resolve_tenant_id → 403 “You cannot access another tenant's data.”
authorize_kb_ids → 404 “Knowledge base not found” (id not named)
Voice WS with a session minted for tenant B’s bot
Onboarding: one txn = tenant + subscription + settings + first admin

svg.text: SHARED VS TENANT-OWNED RESOURCES

Platform-shared (tenant_id NULL / global): provider catalog + models + pricing · languages · industries/regions/plans · AI profiles · guardrail registry · platform voices · global KBs · compliance templates

Tenant-owned: users/team · bots + all studio config (prompts, intents, workflows, channels, voice settings, context schemas) · KBs + documents + chunks · cloned voices · conversations/recordings · usage events · audit slice
Known cross-tenant couplings (verified): Sarvam pronunciation-dictionary quota rides one platform key (10 dicts / 100 words shared) · provider API keys are platform credentials, not per-tenant
Isolation grade: application-enforced row-level scoping on shared infrastructure — no per-tenant databases, schemas or encryption keys exist in the implementation.
